record.context_brief: When the identity lies in a derivation range
record.original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space. For a bounded operator T on H, let δ_T be the inner derivation on L(H) defined by δ_T(X)=TX-XT. For which operators T on H does the identity operator I belong to the norm-closure of the range R(δ_T)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $L(H)$ denote the algebra of bounded linear operators on $H$, equipped with the operator norm. For $T \in L(H)$, the inner derivation implemented by $T$ is the bounded linear map
\[
\delta_T : L(H) \to L(H), \qquad \delta_T(X) = TX - XT.
\]
Its range is $R(\delta_T) = \{TX - XT : X \in L(H)\}$, and $\overline{R(\delta_T)}$ denotes the norm closure of $R(\delta_T)$ in $L(H)$. Let $I \in L(H)$ be the identity operator.

Characterize, intrinsically in terms of the spectral or structural properties of $T$, exactly those operators $T \in L(H)$ for which
\[
I \in \overline{R(\delta_T)}.
\]
(It is known, for instance by results of J. H. Anderson, that if $T$ is normal then $I \notin \overline{R(\delta_T)}$; the problem asks for a complete characterization for general $T \in L(H)$.)
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return a complete intrinsic characterization of operators $T$ with $I \in \overline{R(\delta_T)}$. Classical results (Anderson, Stampfli) give partial obstructions and necessary conditions (e.g. for normal operators $I$ is not in the closure of the range), but a full characterization for arbitrary $T \in L(H)$ does not appear to have been established, and the question is recorded as open in the literature on D-symmetric operators.
